article_title: Distributional Moderation Analysis: Unpacking Moderation Effects in Intervention Research
citation: Wiedermann, W., Reinke, W. M., & Herman, K. C. (2025). Distributional moderation analysis: Unpacking moderation effects in intervention research. Journal of School Psychology, 108. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsp.2024.101399
title: Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management randomized controlled trial dataset (disruptive behavior re-analysis)
description: A cluster-randomized trial evaluating the Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management program, which focuses on effective classroom management practices for preschool and early elementary teachers. As the article states, "The RCT included 1817 students and 105 teachers in kindergarten to third grade from nine schools in a school district in the Midwestern part of the United States." Teachers were randomly assigned to IY TCM training or business as usual; the outcome re-analyzed here is student disruptive behavior measured with the TOCA-C subscale. The dataset serves as the step-by-step illustration of moderated GAMLSS in school-based intervention research.
requirements: Valid baseline and posttreatment measures for the analysis sample
Classroom-level random effects to account for the nested data structure of the cluster randomized design
constraints: The analysis sample included 1628 students (90.0% of the students and 104 teachers) who had valid baseline and posttreatment measures
target_learners: Students in kindergarten through third grade in a Midwestern US school district
target_learning_goals: Reducing students' disruptive classroom behavior through teacher classroom management training
examples: Teachers were randomly assigned to either receive the IY TCM training or business as usual; most students identified as Black (76%), male (52%), and received free/reduced lunch (61%)
key_sources: Wiedermann, W., Reinke, W. M., & Herman, K. C. (2025). Distributional moderation analysis: Unpacking moderation effects in intervention research. Journal of School Psychology, 108. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jsp.2024.101399

article_title: The Incredible Year Teacher Classroom Management Program: Initial Findings from a Group Randomized Control Trial
citation: Reinke, W. M., Herman, K. C., & Dong, N. (2014). The Incredible Year Teacher Classroom Management Program: Initial Findings from a Group Randomized Control Trial. SREE Spring 2014 Conference. https://sree.org
title: Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management (IY TCM) program
description: IY TCM is "a universal classroom management program for teachers of students in grades Kindergarten through third grade." Teachers are trained in small groups across six full days by workshop facilitators, with each workshop building on prior content. Content includes "strategies for increasing proactive teaching, praise and encouragement, incentives, problem solving," and coaching is embedded: a coach conducts observations, provides performance feedback, and assists with goal setting.
requirements: Delivery requires trained IY TCM workshop facilitators across six full days of small-group training plus ongoing individual coaching with observations and performance feedback.
constraints: The program is principle driven and flexible in adapting to each teacher's skill levels and classroom experiences; the trial was conducted in urban, low-income elementary schools.
target_learners: Kindergarten through third grade students in urban low-income elementary schools
target_learning_goals: Student social competence, emotional regulation, and prosocial behavior; teacher proactive classroom management practices
examples: In the trial, 105 teachers were randomized within nine schools across three cohorts; intervention teachers received six workshop days plus weekly coaching, and Table 1 lists workshop topics such as praising, proactive teaching, and teaching self-regulation.
key_sources: Reinke, W. M., Herman, K. C., & Dong, N. (2014). The Incredible Year Teacher Classroom Management Program: Initial Findings from a Group Randomized Control Trial. SREE Spring 2014 Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED563013

article_title: Grade Level Effects of the Incredible Years Teacher Training Program on Emotion Regulation and Attention
citation: Murray, D. W., Rabiner, D. L., & Carrig, M. M. (2014). Grade Level Effects of the Incredible Years Teacher Training Program on Emotion Regulation and Attention. SREE Spring Conference. https://www.sree.org/
title: Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management Program (IYT)
description: IYT is a teacher training program within a series of parent, child, and teacher interventions designed to prevent and treat aggressive behavior and conduct problems in young children aged 3-8 years. Its approach includes "video-modeling, behavioral rehearsal of key skills through numerous role plays, classroom practice assignments, and teacher goal setting and self-monitoring." In the study it was delivered in five monthly full-day workshops led by two trained co-leaders with approximately 12-15 teachers per group, plus two brief classroom consultation visits and regular support emails.
requirements: Trained co-leaders deliver 4-6 monthly full-day workshops; the study used five days averaging 34 training hours with two classroom consultation visits and regular emails
constraints: In the study it was evaluated as an independent intervention in rural early elementary (K-2) settings, whereas prior evidence supported it in combination with other Incredible Years programs
target_learners: K-2 teachers in rural elementary schools
target_learning_goals: Classroom management skills, positive classroom climate, and students' social-emotional competence and achievement
examples: Intervention fidelity was strong, with >85% of workshop objectives met, teacher satisfaction ratings >6 on a 1-7 scale, and a 97% attendance rate
key_sources: Murray, D. W., Rabiner, D. L., & Carrig, M. M. (2014). Grade Level Effects of the Incredible Years Teacher Training Program on Emotion Regulation and Attention. SREE Spring Conference. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED562822

article_title: The Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management Program: Outcomes from a Group Randomized Trial
citation: Wendy M. Reinke & Keith C. Herman & Nianbo Dong. (2018). The Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management Program: Outcomes from a Group Randomized Trial. Prevention Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11121-018-0932-3
title: Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management (IY TCM) program
description: IY TCM is a universal classroom management program for teachers of students in pre-school through third grade. It uses social learning theory via video modeling: teachers view video recordings of effective strategies, role-play their use, and receive feedback from group leaders and peers. The program embeds coaching between sessions, with a coach conducting observations, providing performance feedback, and assisting with problem solving, goal setting, and implementation of strategies.
requirements: Delivered via three sets of two full-day group trainings co-facilitated by doctoral-level IY TCM group leaders supervised by the program developer
Coaching between sessions with observations and individual meetings
constraints: The article notes the program is principle driven and therefore flexible in adapting to the skill levels and specific classroom experiences of each teacher
target_learners: Teachers of students in pre-school through third grade
target_learning_goals: Teacher use of proactive classroom management practices such as behavior-specific praise, positive relationships, pre-corrective statements, teaching classroom expectations, and proximity
examples: In the trial, intervention teachers attended six full-day training sessions with attendance rates of 94–100% and averaged 6 hours of coaching over the year
key_sources: Wendy M. Reinke & Keith C. Herman & Nianbo Dong. (2018). The Incredible Years Teacher Classroom Management Program: Outcomes from a Group Randomized Trial. Prevention Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11121-018-0932-3
